title: DEFINE SHARED variables couple procedures with hidden state — must become explicit parameters or Spring beans, never static fields
sourceContent:
/* post-invoice.p - posts one invoice using shared session context */
DEFINE INPUT PARAMETER piInvNum AS INTEGER NO-UNDO.
DEFINE SHARED VARIABLE gSessionUser AS CHARACTER NO-UNDO.
DEFINE SHARED VARIABLE gPostingDate AS DATE      NO-UNDO.
DEFINE SHARED VARIABLE gLastPosted  AS INTEGER   NO-UNDO.

FIND FIRST Invoice WHERE Invoice.InvNum = piInvNum EXCLUSIVE-LOCK NO-ERROR.
IF AVAILABLE Invoice THEN DO:
    ASSIGN Invoice.Status   = "POSTED"
           Invoice.PostedBy = gSessionUser      /* reads shared state */
           Invoice.PostedOn = gPostingDate.
    gLastPosted = Invoice.InvNum.               /* mutates shared state */
END.
notes: DEFINE SHARED variables are read and written across procedure boundaries with no parameter passing — invisible coupling. gSessionUser/gPostingDate are read; gLastPosted is mutated (a side effect other procedures observe). The Java target must pass these explicitly (method params or a request-scoped bean) and never model them as static mutable fields. The FIND EXCLUSIVE-LOCK is a write-locked managed entity.
